transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lina (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Eric (Verdant VP Eng), Sofia (Verdant ML), Dan (Verdant Security)

Summary: quick qbr to go over usage, cost spikes in Sept, two reliability incidents, roadmap items and dedicated discussion.

Topics: usage trends; cost drivers (gpt-like vs embeddings); reliability incidents (cache exhaustion, region failover); security/compliance questions (KMS, audit logs); Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; next steps and pilot plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lina: okay everyone, thanks for joining, this is the Q4 qbr, um quick intro - I'm Lina from Redwood, Marcus our SE, Priya CSM.
[00:08] Eric: hey thanks, appreciate it. we'll run through where we are.
[00:12] Marcus: cool, so first slide — usage. we saw a steady uptick, right, Sofia you had mentioned the new search feature launched mid-september — did that drive the spike?
[00:21] Sofia: yeah, the search expansion plus the reranker. around sept 12 we had a 2.4x increase in gen traffic, most of it short form chat, embeddings for vector store increased too.
[00:31] Marcus: got it, so tokens per minute rose from ~1.2k to 3k during peak windows. that caused the burst billing.
[00:38] Dan: yeah the cost levers — can you show the cost by route? sometimes embeddings are cheap per op but add up.
[00:44] Lina: absolutely, Marcus will share a per-route breakdown after.
[00:48] [00:50] Marcus: okay flipping to costs — biggest delta was the reranker and a misconfigured timeout that prevented prefix caching; so we were not hitting the KV cache and repeated full-context ops. that alone added about 18% to token usage for September.
[01:04] Sofia: oh right, that timeout was set low in prod for safety then bumped later.
[01:08] Marcus: mm-hmm. also we recommended a small quantized model for reranking but the rollout was delayed.
[01:14] Eric: what's the recommended tradeoff there, latency vs cost? our product needs sub-150ms p95.
[01:19] Marcus: for sub-150ms p95 at your qps, two options: 1) Redwood Dedicated with reserved GPU pools to keep KV in memory and consistent tails; or 2) keep Hosted but enable smarter prefix caching and micro-batching with lower concurrency. Dedicated buys predictability, Hosted buys ease-of-use.
[01:35] Eric: any numbers? like percent cost delta?
[01:38] Marcus: rough ballpark — Dedicated reserved capacity could lower per-token cost by ~20-35% on high sustained qps because of better packing and warm KV caches; Hosted with batching gives you 8-12% improvement usually. numbers vary based on model and sequence length.
[01:52] [02:00] Priya: from ops perspective we can run a short pilot on Dedicated for one service, keep everything else Hosted, so you get a direct apples-to-apples comparison.
[02:08] Eric: that sounds good.
[02:10] Sofia: reliability incidents — we had two in Sept, can we review root cause?
[02:14] Marcus: yes. incident one was around sept 18 — a region-level networking flake and our smart routing fell back to a different variant; there was a short period of higher latency while route convergence happened. we captured traces and the fallback worked but client saw increased p95 for ~6 minutes.
[02:29] Dan: were audit logs available for that window? we need for compliance reviews.
[02:33] Marcus: yes, Redwood Console has request-level traces and audit logs; we'll pull the exact logs and share the slices.
[02:40] Lina: action: we'll export that week of logs with trace ids.
[02:44] [03:05] Eric: second incident?
[03:07] Marcus: cache exhaustion on sept 30 — a test job pushed a large prefix that evicted hot entries; subsequent production requests warmed cold and experienced higher latencies. that was because the per-tenant cache quota was set too low for the new workload. we adjusted quotas and added a guard to reject overly large prefixes.
[03:24] Sofia: phew, okay. can Redwood detect that proactively?
[03:27] Marcus: yep, Redwood Optimize will recommend cache sizing based on observed sequence distribution; plus we can enable alerts.
[03:33] Dan: security — quick check, we're doing customer-managed KMS for keys, right? and do you support HSM?
[03:38] Lina: yes you can bring-your-own KMS, integrate with HSM via our Private deployment option; for Hosted we support envelope encryption and KMS integrations. SOC2 and ISO attestations are on the compliance pack — we'll share the certs.
[03:50] Dan: do logs contain PII? retention policy? we need audit retention for 3 years.
[03:55] Priya: logs can be routed to your SIEM, we offer configurable retention; for Private deployments you control retention fully. we'll send the docs.
[04:02] [04:30] Eric: roadmap — we're planning to roll our multimodal assistant in Q1, which will increase long-context workloads. any guidance on long-context best practices?
[04:38] Marcus: yes, for long context we recommend KV caching of stable prefixes, chunked embeddings, and sequence-aware batching. if you expect sustained long-context traffic, Dedicated or Private can give better performance and cost. also quantized 8-bit for long context helps a lot.
[04:54] Sofia: timeline: ramp starts January, peak in Feb-Mar. can we get a capacity estimate?
[04:59] Marcus: we'll run a sizing exercise; Marcus: (laugh) i'll actually run it — need your expected qps and average context lengths.
[05:05] [05:20] Eric: we're aiming for 2.5k peak concurrent requests with 8k tokens average context during ramp.
[05:27] Marcus: ok that's helpful. we'll prepare a Dedicated sizing workshop and a cost model.
[05:33] Lina: quick pricing ask — can you provide a committed reserved capacity quote vs pay-as-you-go for a 12-month term?
[05:40] Priya: yes we can. I'll work with finance to get a committed tier quote; we'll include burst policies.
[05:44] Eric: what about SLAs around latency?
[05:48] Marcus: SLA is tiered; Dedicated gives you higher uptime and latency SLOs. for p95 latency SLOs we can attach monitoring probes and provide remediation windows. we'll align on the SLO you need and put into the contract addendum.
[06:00] [06:30] Sofia: integration notes — we use Kubernetes ingress and have private subnets; if we go Private we need air-gapped deploy playbook.
[06:37] Lina: understood. we have an on-prem packaging process and network diagrams; we'll share the playbook and an estimated timeline for Private.
[06:44] Dan: also SAML SSO, RBAC mapping — can Redwood sync with our IdP?
[06:49] Priya: yes SAML and SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC roles are configurable. we'll include a sample mapping.
[06:55] [07:20] Marcus: one more ops note — we saw some tokenization differences between the open model variant and the smaller quantized variant you tried; keep an eye for subtle regression. Redwood Optimize has eval hooks to run prompt regression tests automatically.
[07:35] Sofia: good, we definitely want automated regressions.
[07:38] Eric: for the pilot — what's the minimal timebox to get meaningful numbers?
[07:44] Marcus: i'd say 2 weeks of production traffic on Dedicated for the reranker route should be enough to compare p95 and cost delta. include some controlled load tests for peak.
[07:53] Eric: ok let's plan that.
[08:00] [30:00] [note: middle of call included interactive Q/A and screenshare, some timestamps omitted for brevity]
[40:10] Dan: around compliance, can you provide a SOC2 type II summary and the encryption architecture diagram?
[40:16] Lina: yes, we'll attach the compliance pack and an architecture diagram in the follow up.
[40:22] Marcus: also, we'll include traces for the sept 18 incident and eviction window.
[40:28] Sofia: great. on billing, can we get a sample month-by-month cost projection if we move reranker to Dedicated?
[40:35] Priya: we'll model three scenarios: baseline (current), partial Dedicated (reranker only), full Dedicated for gen services.
[40:42] Eric: and include burst allowances.
[40:45] Priya: yes.
[41:00] [50:00] Marcus: last item — a small engineering ask: can Redwood offer a read-only Kinesis/stream of request metadata for our observability pipeline?
[41:08] Lina: we can expose logs to your SIEM and we have streaming hooks for events; i'll confirm the format.
[41:14] Dan: perfect.
[41:18] Lina: recap and next steps: Marcus will send per-route cost spreadsheet and incident logs; Priya will coordinate Dedicated sizing workshop and committed pricing; Eric to confirm SLA target and internal stakeholders.
[41:30] Eric: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[41:33] Lina: thanks all.

End of transcript.
